headline: Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel-winning AI pioneer, proposed that AI companies should have to prove their models are safe to a regulator before release, as drugmakers do with the FDA.
score_reason: Pool score kept: prominent voice, concrete regulatory proposal, but a proposal only.
importance_line: A proposal from one of AI's best-known scientists could shape the safety debate for the public and lawmakers, but it is only a proposal and no regulator has acted on it.
source: Business Insider, as republished by AOL.com
summary: Business Insider reports, in an article republished by AOL.com, that Hinton, often called the "Godfather of AI", said on the "Smart Girl Dumb Questions" podcast on 6 Oct 2026 that AI firms should convince a regulator their products are safe before release, the way drugmakers must with the US Food and Drug Administration. He warned that AI now helps improve itself, and said he guessed "we have a year or two before everything gets much worse", adding that it is "just a guess".
notes: Page text looks like a Business Insider article republished by AOL (it quotes 'told Business Insider') but the page does not say so; credited to AOL.com. Mentions OpenAI shelving GPT-6.1 Astra after safety tests; only as context.
